newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Chavalit administration has declared war on PollWatch with the prime minister calling its chief childish and the PM's secretary-general asking the election watchdog to move its office off a government property. The moves come in the wake of PollWatch's relentless campaign to bring Chavalit and some other government politicians to trial for alleged electoral offences. (THE NATION)

- Bureaucratic reform will be completed in three months, leaving the government free to concentrate on real legitimate tasks such as defence and courts, the judicial process, foreign and financial affairs, says Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. He also expresses confidence the Thai economy, currently blighted by a high current account deficit, instability in financial markets and liquidity shortages in the property sector, would pick up and return to its prosperous track. (BANGKOK POST)

- Young blood MPs have opposed the Constitution Drafting Assembly's (CDA) plan to require that MPs resign if they are appointed Cabinet ministers, reasoning that it would limit their role and have negative consequences on the political system. (THE NATION)

- Next month's meeting of the Board of Investment (BOI) will discuss revision of the formula for calculating tax rebates for automotive assemblers in a bid to enhance car exports. Industry Minister Korn Dabaransi says he has been assigned by the Prime Minister's Office Minister, Weerakorn Khamprakorb, to prepare information for the revision. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thai-owned oil trading company Cosmo Group has unveiled a 2 billion baht plan to tap the recently-liberalised Philippine retail oil market in partnership with Philippine firms. The Philippine partners are in the real estate and banking sectors in addition to a group which controls the local McDonald's fast food business. (THE NATION)

- The process of granting 28 new insurance licences has come under fire from a former deputy premier and the spokesman for the House Economic Standing Committee. They have questioned whether the licence bidders approved by the cabinet had been selected openly. The committee will discuss the issue next week. (BANGKOK POST)
